_comment: DRAFT in-game context help for every opcode, for antony to edit; drafted by Claude from opcode.hpp, machine.cpp and game/docs/machine_language.md. Presentation only: nothing the simulation reads. Keys are the bare save-format names (OPCODE_NAMES minus the OPCODE_ prefix, as in assets.json and the OPCODE::X reader), in opcode.hpp order. Per entry: 'name' is the display name, 'summary' a one-line tooltip, 'help' a few sentences, 'stack' the stack effect as before -- after with the top of stack rightmost (omitted where the stack is untouched). Loaded at startup into a lookup (game/presentation.hpp); no UI shows it yet (the hover help panel is a later todo). A unit test requires an entry for every opcode and no entry for an unknown one.

NOOP.name: No-Op
NOOP.summary: Does nothing; the truck drives straight on.
NOOP.help: Does nothing. The truck carries straight on. Useful as a placeholder or a marker on a track.

SKIP.name: Skip
SKIP.summary: Drive over the next cell without using it.
SKIP.help: The next cell is ignored: its instruction is not run and any number there is not picked up. Use it to cross another track's instructions or data. Other trucks, valves and junctions still block the way, and a skipped valve or flip-flop does not flip.

HALT.name: Halt
HALT.summary: Stop here until this cell changes.
HALT.help: The truck parks on this cell and waits, keeping its stack. When the cell is changed (for example you replace the tile), the truck wakes and runs whatever is there now. Trucks behind it queue up.

TURN_NORTH.name: Turn North
TURN_NORTH.summary: Face north, whichever way the truck was going.
TURN_NORTH.help: The truck turns to face north and leaves that way, wherever it came from. Good for merging tracks: trucks arriving from any side all leave north. If that means reversing, the truck pauses briefly to turn round.

TURN_EAST.name: Turn East
TURN_EAST.summary: Face east, whichever way the truck was going.
TURN_EAST.help: The truck turns to face east and leaves that way, wherever it came from. Good for merging tracks: trucks arriving from any side all leave east. If that means reversing, the truck pauses briefly to turn round.

TURN_SOUTH.name: Turn South
TURN_SOUTH.summary: Face south, whichever way the truck was going.
TURN_SOUTH.help: The truck turns to face south and leaves that way, wherever it came from. Good for merging tracks: trucks arriving from any side all leave south. If that means reversing, the truck pauses briefly to turn round.

TURN_WEST.name: Turn West
TURN_WEST.summary: Face west, whichever way the truck was going.
TURN_WEST.help: The truck turns to face west and leaves that way, wherever it came from. Good for merging tracks: trucks arriving from any side all leave west. If that means reversing, the truck pauses briefly to turn round.

TURN_RIGHT.name: Turn Right
TURN_RIGHT.summary: Turn a quarter-turn to the right.
TURN_RIGHT.help: The truck turns right (clockwise) and carries on. Four right turns make a loop.

TURN_LEFT.name: Turn Left
TURN_LEFT.summary: Turn a quarter-turn to the left.
TURN_LEFT.help: The truck turns left (anticlockwise) and carries on.

TURN_BACK.name: Turn Back
TURN_BACK.summary: Turn round and go back the way you came.
TURN_BACK.help: The truck reverses and leaves the way it came in, after a short pause to turn round.

BRANCH_RIGHT.name: Branch Right
BRANCH_RIGHT.summary: Take the top number; turn right that many times.
BRANCH_RIGHT.help: Takes the number on top of the stack and turns right that many quarter-turns: 0 goes straight, 1 turns right, 2 turns back, -1 turns left. True counts as 1 and false as 0, so a comparison can steer it directly. If the top is not a number (or the stack is empty) the truck goes straight and keeps its stack.

BRANCH_LEFT.name: Branch Left
BRANCH_LEFT.summary: Take the top number; turn left that many times.
BRANCH_LEFT.help: Takes the number on top of the stack and turns left that many quarter-turns: 0 goes straight, 1 turns left, 2 turns back, -1 turns right. True counts as 1 and false as 0, so a comparison can steer it directly. If the top is not a number (or the stack is empty) the truck goes straight and keeps its stack.

LOAD.name: Load
LOAD.summary: Pick up what is on the next cell.
LOAD.help: Puts whatever is on the next cell on top of the stack, without running it. Numbers and instruction tiles are copied and stay where they are; cargo is taken, leaving the cell empty. An empty cell gives nothing.

STORE.name: Store
STORE.summary: Put the top of the stack onto the next cell.
STORE.help: Takes the top of the stack and writes it onto the next cell, replacing any number or instruction there. Cargo is never destroyed: if the cell holds cargo, or you are putting down cargo and the cell is not empty, the truck waits on that cell until it clears. Gotcha: with an empty stack, STORE erases the next cell.

EXCHANGE.name: Exchange
EXCHANGE.summary: Swap the top of the stack with the next cell.
EXCHANGE.help: Takes the top of the stack, picks up what is on the next cell, and leaves the first thing there in its place. Nothing is copied or lost, so it works on cargo too. With an empty stack it just picks up the cell's contents, leaving it empty. Unlike STORE it never waits, so it can put cargo down on top of an instruction.

HEADING_LOAD.name: Heading Load
HEADING_LOAD.summary: Push the direction the truck is facing.
HEADING_LOAD.help: Puts the truck's heading on the stack: 0 north, 1 east, 2 south, 3 west. Gotcha: the number counts every turn, so each full clockwise lap adds 4. BITWISE AND with 3 gives the direction 0-3; SHIFT RIGHT by 2 counts laps.

HEADING_STORE.name: Heading Store
HEADING_STORE.summary: Take the top number and face that direction.
HEADING_STORE.help: Takes the number on top of the stack and faces that way: 0 north, 1 east, 2 south, 3 west (other numbers wrap round). If the top is not a number the truck goes straight and keeps its stack. Gotcha: the numbers are compass directions, so rotating or mirroring a blueprint does not change where they point.

LOCATION_LOAD.name: Location Load
LOCATION_LOAD.help: Planned to put the truck's location on the stack. Not working yet: the truck drives straight over it, as over a No-Op.

LOCATION_STORE.name: Location Store
LOCATION_STORE.help: Reserved; not working. The truck drives straight over it, as over a No-Op.

DROP.name: Drop
DROP.summary: Throw away the top of the stack (cargo: put it down).
DROP.help: Throws away the top of the stack. Cargo is never destroyed: instead the truck drives onto the next cell and puts it down there, as if by STORE, waiting on that cell until it is empty. Gotcha: when dropping cargo, the next cell's instruction is not run.

DUPLICATE.name: Duplicate
DUPLICATE.summary: Copy the top of the stack.
DUPLICATE.help: Puts a second copy of the top item on the stack. Cargo cannot be copied: if the top is cargo, nothing happens.

SWAP.name: Swap
SWAP.help: Exchanges the top two items on the stack. Works on anything, including cargo. Does nothing with fewer than two items.

OVER.name: Over
OVER.summary: Copy the second item onto the top.
OVER.help: Puts a copy of the item just under the top onto the stack. Cargo cannot be copied, so nothing happens if that item is cargo, or if there are fewer than two items.

IS_ZERO.name: Is Zero
IS_ZERO.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is zero, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

IS_POSITIVE.name: Is Positive
IS_POSITIVE.summary: Is the top number above zero?
IS_POSITIVE.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is greater than zero (zero is not positive), false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

IS_NEGATIVE.name: Is Negative
IS_NEGATIVE.summary: Is the top number below zero?
IS_NEGATIVE.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is less than zero, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

IS_NOT_ZERO.name: Is Not Zero
IS_NOT_ZERO.summary: Is the top number anything but zero?
IS_NOT_ZERO.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is not zero, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

IS_NOT_POSITIVE.name: Is Not Positive
IS_NOT_POSITIVE.summary: Is the top number zero or below?
IS_NOT_POSITIVE.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is zero or less, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

IS_NOT_NEGATIVE.name: Is Not Negative
IS_NOT_NEGATIVE.summary: Is the top number zero or above?
IS_NOT_NEGATIVE.help: Replaces the number on top with true if it is zero or more, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

LOGICAL_NOT.name: Logical Not
LOGICAL_NOT.help: Replaces the top with its opposite: true becomes false and false becomes true. Numbers work too: 0 counts as false, anything else as true. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

LOGICAL_AND.name: Logical And
LOGICAL_AND.summary: True if both of the top two are true.
LOGICAL_AND.help: Replaces the top two with true if both are true, false otherwise. 0 counts as false, any other number as true. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

LOGICAL_OR.name: Logical Or
LOGICAL_OR.summary: True if either of the top two is true.
LOGICAL_OR.help: Replaces the top two with true if either (or both) is true, false otherwise. 0 counts as false, any other number as true. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

LOGICAL_XOR.name: Logical Xor
LOGICAL_XOR.summary: True if exactly one of the top two is true.
LOGICAL_XOR.help: Replaces the top two with true if exactly one of them is true, false if both or neither are. 0 counts as false, any other number as true. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

BITWISE_NOT.name: Bitwise Not
BITWISE_NOT.summary: Flip every bit of the top number.
BITWISE_NOT.help: Flips every bit of the top number. The result is minus one minus the number, so 0 becomes -1 and 5 becomes -6. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

BITWISE_AND.name: Bitwise And
BITWISE_AND.summary: Keep the bits set in both numbers.
BITWISE_AND.help: Replaces the top two numbers with the bits set in both. AND with 3 keeps the last two bits, which turns a heading back into 0-3. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

BITWISE_OR.name: Bitwise Or
BITWISE_OR.summary: Keep the bits set in either number.
BITWISE_OR.help: Replaces the top two numbers with the bits set in either one. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

BITWISE_XOR.name: Bitwise Xor
BITWISE_XOR.summary: Keep the bits set in exactly one number.
BITWISE_XOR.help: Replaces the top two numbers with the bits set in one but not the other. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

BITWISE_SPLIT.name: Bitwise Split
BITWISE_SPLIT.summary: Split two numbers into shared and unshared bits.
BITWISE_SPLIT.help: Replaces the top two numbers with two results: the bits set in both (underneath) and the bits set in just one (on top). No bits are lost; it is the building block of binary addition. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

SHIFT_RIGHT.name: Shift Right
SHIFT_RIGHT.summary: Halve a number n times (n on top).
SHIFT_RIGHT.help: Shifts the lower number right by the top number of bits: each step halves it, rounding down. A negative count acts as 0, and counts above 60 act as 60. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

POPCOUNT.name: Popcount
POPCOUNT.summary: Count the 1 bits in the top number.
POPCOUNT.help: Replaces the top number with how many of its bits are 1. Gotcha: negative numbers count their sign bits too, so -1 gives 64. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

ABS.name: Abs
ABS.help: Replaces the top number with its size, dropping any minus sign: -5 becomes 5. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

NEGATE.name: Negate
NEGATE.summary: Flip the sign of the top number.
NEGATE.help: Replaces the top number with its negative: 5 becomes -5 and -5 becomes 5. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

SIGN.name: Sign
SIGN.summary: Replace the top number with -1, 0 or 1.
SIGN.help: Replaces the top number with -1 if it is negative, 0 if zero, 1 if positive. Feed it to a branch to turn left, go straight or turn right. Does nothing if the top is not a number.

ADD.name: Add
ADD.help: Replaces the top two numbers with their sum. Gotcha: results beyond about 576 quadrillion (either sign) stop counting as numbers, and later instructions ignore them. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

SUBTRACT.name: Subtract
SUBTRACT.summary: Subtract the top number from the one below.
SUBTRACT.help: Replaces the top two numbers with the lower one minus the top one. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

EQUAL.name: Equal
EQUAL.summary: Are the top two items the same?
EQUAL.help: Replaces the top two items with true if they are equal, false otherwise. Numbers, true/false (as 1/0) and instruction tiles can all be compared; things of different kinds are never equal. Cargo cannot be compared: if either item is cargo, or the stack has fewer than two items, nothing happens.

NOT_EQUAL.name: Not Equal
NOT_EQUAL.summary: Are the top two items different?
NOT_EQUAL.help: Replaces the top two items with true if they differ, false if they are equal. Numbers, true/false (as 1/0) and instruction tiles can all be compared; things of different kinds always differ. Cargo cannot be compared: if either item is cargo, or the stack has fewer than two items, nothing happens.

LESS_THAN.name: Less Than
LESS_THAN.summary: Is the lower number less than the top one?
LESS_THAN.help: Replaces the top two numbers with true if the lower one is less than the top one, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

GREATER_THAN.name: Greater Than
GREATER_THAN.summary: Is the lower number greater than the top one?
GREATER_THAN.help: Replaces the top two numbers with true if the lower one is greater than the top one, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.name: Less Than Or Equal To
LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.summary: Is the lower number at most the top one?
LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.help: Replaces the top two numbers with true if the lower one is less than or equal to the top one, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.name: Greater Than Or Equal To
GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.summary: Is the lower number at least the top one?
GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO.help: Replaces the top two numbers with true if the lower one is greater than or equal to the top one, false otherwise. True and false count as 1 and 0 wherever a number is wanted, so the result can steer a branch directly. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

COMPARE.name: Compare
COMPARE.help: Replaces the top two numbers with -1 if the lower one is smaller, 0 if they are equal, 1 if it is larger. Feed it to a branch to turn left, go straight or turn right. Does nothing unless the top two are both numbers.

FLIP_FLOP.name: Flip Flop
FLIP_FLOP.summary: Turn right, then become a Flop Flip.
FLIP_FLOP.help: The truck turns right, and the tile changes itself into a FLOP FLIP, so the next truck turns left. A stream of trucks is split alternately right and left. Skipping or loading it does not flip it.

FLOP_FLIP.name: Flop Flip
FLOP_FLIP.summary: Turn left, then become a Flip Flop.
FLOP_FLIP.help: The truck turns left, and the tile changes itself into a FLIP FLOP, so the next truck turns right. A stream of trucks is split alternately left and right. Skipping or loading it does not flip it.

ROT.name: Rot
ROT.summary: Bring the third item up to the top.
ROT.help: Takes the third item from the top and puts it on top, moving the other two down one. Works on anything, including cargo. Does nothing with fewer than three items.
ROT.stack: x y z -- y z x

IS_MATTER.name: Is Matter
IS_MATTER.summary: Is the top item cargo? (keeps the item)
IS_MATTER.help: Puts true on the stack if the top item is cargo, false if it is anything else. The item itself stays where it was, underneath the answer. Does nothing on an empty stack.

VALVE_NORTH_SOUTH.name: Valve North-South
VALVE_NORTH_SOUTH.summary: Gate open north-south; flips when driven through.
VALVE_NORTH_SOUTH.help: Trucks can only pass travelling north or south; trucks arriving from east or west wait in front of it. Each truck that drives through flips it to East-West, closing it behind itself. A valve never turns a truck, and one that Skips over it does not flip it.

VALVE_EAST_WEST.name: Valve East-West
VALVE_EAST_WEST.summary: Gate open east-west; flips when driven through.
VALVE_EAST_WEST.help: Trucks can only pass travelling east or west; trucks arriving from north or south wait in front of it. Each truck that drives through flips it to North-South, closing it behind itself. A valve never turns a truck, and one that Skips over it does not flip it.

DO_NOT_QUEUE.name: Do Not Queue
DO_NOT_QUEUE.summary: Junction: only enter if you can drive straight out.
DO_NOT_QUEUE.help: A truck only enters this cell when the cell straight beyond it is free too, and claims both at once. So no truck ever stops on the junction, and cross traffic keeps flowing while others wait. It never turns a truck.

MINE.name: Mine
MINE.summary: Dig the ground under the next cell for cargo.
MINE.help: On reaching the next cell the truck stops to dig, then puts one item of that ground's material (sand, rock, coal...) on its stack. Harder ground takes longer. Unlike LOAD, the next cell's instruction or number is still used after digging. Ground with no material gives nothing.

BURY.name: Bury
BURY.summary: Return cargo to matching ground under next cell.
BURY.help: On reaching the next cell the truck stops to dig, and if the top of its stack is cargo of that ground's own kind, puts it back into the ground. Anything else stays on the stack and the digging time is wasted. The next cell is still used as normal afterwards.

DUMP.name: Dump
DUMP.summary: Turn back and unload the top item behind you.
DUMP.help: The truck turns round and puts the top of its stack into the cell it was heading for, such as a Ship's hold. It waits, turned round, until that cell is empty. With an empty stack it just turns round. A Ship only sells priced cargo: anything else stays in the hold and blocks it.
